# FlatZinc checker coverage

This is the finite target for the full-support expansion, not a claim that the
current checker accepts these libraries. The [checker guide](../crates/zincite-check/README.md)
describes working behavior. Every direct mathematical operation below has one
family owner. Source wrappers and compiler intrinsics belong to the profile
that must lower them; their emitted operations belong to the direct families.
No source wrapper, feature flag or missing include counts as implemented support.

Read the [family semantics](#family-semantics-and-completion),
[grammar and numeric boundaries](#grammar-metadata-and-numeric-boundaries),
[external hooks](#external-hooks), [registry](#registry-and-exact-aliases),
[include index](#include-and-selection-index), and
[source signatures](#source-signatures-and-decomposition-calls).
The [name index](#extracted-totals-and-name-index) locates overloads; `D` rows name
source declarations and `R` rows name active registry statements.

The sections above the generated marker are authored policy and semantic notes.
The name, registry, include and signature tables below it are generated; review
the helper and regenerate them instead of editing individual rows.

| Source | Fixed identity | Inventory root |

| Gecode main checked 2026-10-26 | `186551447db0f74639d65cb8de5af190f15ac2c2` | `gecode/flatzinc/mznlib` and `gecode/flatzinc/registry.cpp` |

The linked sources also supply the
[FlatZinc grammar](https://github.com/MiniZinc/libminizinc/blob/c3448c48e7f05f13805616cfd1b9e94972eef58c/docs/en/fzn-grammar.mzn),

Signatures and call heads are an index into those sources. Checking semantics
come from mathematical definitions, decomposition bodies, registry handlers and
the native operation they invoke; introductory comments alone are insufficient.
MiniZinc's [license](https://github.com/MiniZinc/libminizinc/blob/c3448c48e7f05f13805616cfd1b9e94972eef58c/LICENSE.txt)
and Gecode's [license and file author notices](https://github.com/Gecode/gecode/blob/186551447db0f74639d65cb8de5af190f15ac2c2/LICENSE)
apply to the upstream declarations.

Run from this checkout, passing clean Git roots at the exact commits:

```sh
uv run scripts/checker-coverage.py target/checker-upstream/minizinc-2.10.1 target/checker-upstream/gecode-main
```

The helper verifies both Git identities and clean source trees, scans balanced
MiniZinc items without treating comments or strings as declarations, resolves
both include profiles, expands registry aliases literally, checks task assignment,
and compares the generated tables. It also checks the admission names in
`Lowerer::constraint` and `ArithmeticOperation::from_name`. `--write` updates only the generated section after source
and ownership review. The helper needs Python 3.11 or newer and no dependencies.
It does not compile a model or certify runtime semantics.

For this inventory, the GitHub connector supplied individual source text. Its
text-only API cannot fetch binary archives, so two fresh ignored local Git roots
were fetched read-only at the exact commits. No upstream code was executed.
To reproduce the source acquisition in an empty destination:

```sh
mkdir -p target/checker-upstream
git init target/checker-upstream/minizinc-2.10.1
git -C target/checker-upstream/minizinc-2.10.1 fetch --depth=1 https://github.com/MiniZinc/libminizinc.git c3448c48e7f05f13805616cfd1b9e94972eef58c
git -C target/checker-upstream/minizinc-2.10.1 checkout --detach FETCH_HEAD
git init target/checker-upstream/gecode-main
git -C target/checker-upstream/gecode-main fetch --depth=1 https://github.com/Gecode/gecode.git 186551447db0f74639d65cb8de5af190f15ac2c2
git -C target/checker-upstream/gecode-main checkout --detach FETCH_HEAD
```

## Current support

`C` means the exact call spelling and admitted argument types work. Text
preparation also accepts matching bodyless declarations with arbitrary formal
names, fixed/open array shapes and literal domain restrictions. It does not
admit entire upstream source files. Fixed arguments can fill variable
slots. Arrays use the current one-dimensional `1..n` model representation.
All other mathematical calls and aliases are planned work.

| Current exact name | Additional admission limits | Current deterministic output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `int_lin_eq(a,x,c)` | Fixed i64 coefficients/bound; equal array lengths | One output occurrence with nonzero coefficient and exact division |
| `int_lin_le(a,x,c)` | Same fixed/shape limits | None |
| `int_le_reif(x,y,b)` | Two integer operands and a Boolean result | `b` |
| `set_in(x,s)` | Integer and fixed/variable finite integer set | None |
| `set_eq(s,t)` | Finite integer sets | Either set if its output occurs once |
| `set_subset(s,t)` | Finite integer sets | None |
| `set_card(s,n)` | Checked i64 cardinality | `n` |
| `set_union(s,t,r)` | Compact finite integer sets | `r`, absent from the inputs |
| `set_intersect(s,t,r)` | Compact finite integer sets | `r`, absent from the inputs |
| `fzn_disjunctive_strict(start,duration)` | Equal array lengths; fixed nonnegative durations; matching bodyless declaration; formal names can vary | None |
| `int_abs(x,r)`, `int_negate(x,r)` | Checked i64 absolute value/negation; also each exact `gecode_` and `fzn_` prefix | `r`, absent from the input |
| `int_plus(x,y,r)`, `int_minus(x,y,r)`, `int_times(x,y,r)`, `int_div(x,y,r)`, `int_mod(x,y,r)`, `int_min(x,y,r)`, `int_max(x,y,r)` | Checked i64 operands/results; also each exact `gecode_` and `fzn_` prefix | `r`, absent from both inputs |
| `int_pow(x,y,r)` | Variable or fixed integer exponent | `r`, absent from both inputs |
| `int_pow_fixed(x,y,r)` | Fixed integer exponent, including negative values | `r`, absent from the base |
| `gecode_int_pow(x,y,r)`, `gecode_gecode_int_pow(x,y,r)`, `fzn_gecode_int_pow(x,y,r)` | Fixed exponent in `0..2147483646` | `r`, absent from the base |

The `fzn_disjunctive_strict` declaration is required for that external call.
The other listed names accept calls without declarations. All matching declarations
validate signatures, roles and shapes, with call checks for declared domains and
lengths. Current evidence is
[`Lowerer::constraint` and `strict_disjunctive`](../crates/zincite-check/src/prepare.rs),
[annotation validation](../crates/zincite-check/src/prepare/annotations.rs),
[`Predicate` and `definition_direction`](../crates/zincite-check/src/lib.rs), and
[serialized operand validation](../crates/zincite-check/src/serialized.rs).
Preparation, execution and loading must all support an operation before its row
can change to `C`; an enum case alone is insufficient.

## Family semantics and completion

The following sections define the owner and useful output rule referenced by
every direct row. Positions are one-based. `defines_var` may calculate only a
specified unique output from available inputs. Full reification calculates its
Boolean truth value; ordinary implication does not calculate its guard. A supplied
output is checked as supplied, and a derived value outside its domain feeds later
checks. Missing values produce blocked checks independently of known violations.
The indexed signature supplies exact argument order and fixed/variable roles.

<a id="family-011"></a>
**checker-011 — text structure and annotations.** Admit the grammar and metadata
classes below, match declaration signatures by types and argument roles, validate
aliases, and issue located errors for unsupported semantics. Formal parameter
spelling must no longer restrict signatures.

<a id="family-012"></a>
**checker-012 — integer arithmetic.** `abs`, addition, subtraction, negation,
multiplication, division, modulus, min/max and power calculate their final output.
`int_minus(x,y,z)` means `z=x-y`; `int_negate(x,y)` means `y=-x`.
Integer division truncates toward zero; modulus follows `x=(x div y)*y + x mod y`.
The standard negative-exponent contract is `1 div pow(x,abs(y))`.
Division truncates toward zero and modulus has the dividend's sign.
Zero divisors, `MIN / -1`, absolute value/negation of `MIN`, and intermediate
overflow are located execution errors; `MIN mod -1` is zero. Power uses checked
exponentiation by squaring: `0^0 = 1`, a negative power of zero is an error, and
`(-2)^63 = MIN` fits. Standard negative powers check the exponent magnitude and
the denominator before division, so an exponent of `MIN` or denominator overflow
is an error even when an unbounded calculation would truncate to zero. Standard
exponents have no u32 cutoff; bases `0`, `1` and `-1` support large magnitudes.
`int_pow` accepts a variable exponent; `int_pow_fixed` requires a parameter.
Gecode native power requires a fixed exponent in `0..2147483646`, from the pinned
[`Int::Limits::max`](https://github.com/Gecode/gecode/blob/186551447db0f74639d65cb8de5af190f15ac2c2/gecode/int/limits.hpp#L68).
The literal registry prefixes on `gecode_int_pow` produce only
`gecode_gecode_int_pow` and `fzn_gecode_int_pow`; `fzn_int_pow` is unsupported.
Read both `flatzinc_builtins.mzn` and `redefinitions-2.2.1.mzn`; the standard
power wrappers and Gecode's fixed-exponent native call have separate contracts.

<a id="family-013"></a>
**checker-013 — integer comparisons and linear forms.** Check `=`, `!=`, `<`,
`<=`, `>` and `>=`, including the actual reified and implication forms. Integer
relation codes are `1 =`, `2 !=`, `3 <=`, `4 <`, `5 >=`, `6 >`
([handler](https://github.com/Gecode/gecode/blob/186551447db0f74639d65cb8de5af190f15ac2c2/gecode/flatzinc/registry.cpp#L1810)).
Equality can define either unique scalar slot; linear equality can define one
single-occurrence nonzero-coefficient slot by exact division. Inequalities and
reified integer operands do not supply arbitrary values. Validate array lengths,
fixed coefficients/bounds and repeated output occurrences.

<a id="family-014"></a>
**checker-014 — Boolean logic and Boolean linear forms.** Check truth tables,
left/right implication, clauses, comparisons, reductions and `bool2int` (`false=0`,
`true=1`). A Boolean result, Boolean complement/channel or exact linear equality
slot is useful when uniquely determined. Empty AND is true; empty OR and XOR are
false. Standard `array_bool_xor(x)` requires odd parity; the Gecode reduction
handlers also accept `(x,b)` and equate `b` with parity. Their one-array forms
require a true reduction result. Standard Boolean linear bounds and Gecode's
variable-bound declarations are separate signatures. The functional operators
`bool_left_imp(x,y,b)` and `bool_right_imp(x,y,b)` calculate argument 3 as
`b = (y -> x)` and `b = (x -> y)` respectively; their final Boolean is a result.

The pinned `p_array_bool_clause_imp` calls the same `clause(...,b)` overload as
`p_array_bool_clause_reif`
([lines 650–663](https://github.com/Gecode/gecode/blob/186551447db0f74639d65cb8de5af190f15ac2c2/gecode/flatzinc/registry.cpp#L650)).
That handler imposes equivalence, whereas ordinary `_imp` semantics require only
`b -> clause`. This exact spelling appears only in Gecode's redefinitions at this
pin; the standard builtins do not declare it. The registry rows record the actual
binding. checker-014 must document this Gecode-specific discrepancy alongside
ordinary guarded implication; it must not infer behavior from the suffix or
silently change every implication to equivalence.

<a id="family-015"></a>
**checker-015 — finite floats and core relations.** Add scalar/linear comparisons,
absolute value, addition, multiplication, division, min/max, `int2float`, fixed
float-set/domain membership and ceil/floor/round. Arithmetic/conversion outputs
use the final slot; reified comparisons calculate their Boolean. The numeric
policy below must settle tolerance, strict inequalities, conversion ties,
overflow, undefined operations and nonfinite results before these rows work.
Gecode float relation codes use the same six comparisons as integer codes
([handler](https://github.com/Gecode/gecode/blob/186551447db0f74639d65cb8de5af190f15ac2c2/gecode/flatzinc/registry.cpp#L2987)).

<a id="family-016"></a>
**checker-016 — elements and conditionals.** A known index or condition selects
the result without demanding unselected values. Standard element calls use
one-based arrays; nonshifted and Gecode offset forms preserve their declared
index sets. Integer/Boolean two-dimensional handlers take row, column, flattened
row-major values and two index sets; the set two-dimensional handler instead
takes values, zero-based column, width, zero-based row, height, result. Check
bounds, positive dimensions and flattened lengths, not just a matching arity
([handlers](https://github.com/Gecode/gecode/blob/186551447db0f74639d65cb8de5af190f15ac2c2/gecode/flatzinc/registry.cpp#L695)).

<a id="family-017"></a>
**checker-017 — finite-set primitives.** Check membership, cardinality, equality,
disequality, subset/superset, lexicographic comparisons and exact set algebra,
including the actual reified/implication variants. Algebra/cardinality calculate
their result; set equality can calculate either set. Comparisons choose no
members. `int_in` compatibility handlers also accept Boolean variables interpreted
as 0/1 against a fixed integer set. With set variables disabled, `set_in` aliases
only that fixed-set handler; with them enabled it uses the set handler.

The actual [set-code switch](https://github.com/Gecode/gecode/blob/186551447db0f74639d65cb8de5af190f15ac2c2/gecode/flatzinc/registry.cpp#L2649)
accepts `1 =`, `2 !=`, `3 subset`, `4 superset`, `5 disjoint`, `6 complement`,
`7 lex <=`, `8 lex <`, `9 lex >=`, `10 lex >`. This extends the introductory
comment's codes 1–4. Complement uses Gecode's finite set universe below.

<a id="family-018"></a>
**checker-018 — float functions.** Cover sqrt, powers, exp, logarithms,
trigonometric/inverse trigonometric and hyperbolic/inverse hyperbolic functions,
and float array extrema. Each forward result is unique on its defined domain;
array extrema require nonempty arrays. Standard `array_float_minimum(m,xs)` and
`array_float_maximum(m,xs)` calculate argument 1; Gecode's
`gecode_float_array_min(xs,y)` and `gecode_float_array_max(xs,y)` calculate the
final argument. Gecode's integer exponent is fixed and
nonnegative, while its fixed-base power requires a positive base. The MPFR guard
on a registration changes upstream availability, not this task's obligation.
`float_cosh`, `float_sinh` and `float_tanh` occur in commented registration lines;
the Gecode redefinitions decompose them through `exp` and arithmetic. All three
still have standard direct-operation and profile-decomposition owners.

<a id="family-019"></a>
**checker-019 — counts and distributions.** Count occurrences, position-wise
matches, membership and distinct values; check exact/at-least/at-most forms,
sliding windows and open/closed global cardinalities. An equality can calculate
its count or count array from known entries. A count inequality, lower/upper bound
or window bound does not determine a count variable uniquely. Respect the exact
order of count/value/array arguments and relation codes in each declaration.

<a id="family-020"></a>
**checker-020 — order, distinctness and integer channels.** Check lexicographic
array order/disequality, pairwise distinctness/equality (optional, excluded-value
and offset forms), increasing/decreasing order, membership, precedence, sorting,
inverse and integer/Boolean channels. Sorted arrays, extrema, and a complete
inverse/channel side can be unique outputs. Extremum indexes with `break_ties=true`
use the first extremum plus offset; with it false, ties permit several indexes,
so do not choose one. Distinctness, order, membership and precedence alone have no
chosen witness output. This family also owns the mathematical decreasing
operations on the missing legacy include paths described below.

<a id="family-021"></a>
**checker-021 — integer/Boolean tables.** Check tuple membership against flattened
row-major tuples, with exact width and shape validation. Reification can calculate
its Boolean; table membership does not choose a tuple or a missing tuple element.
The registry distinguishes full reification and guarded implication.

<a id="family-022"></a>
**checker-022 — automata.** Check DFA and NFA acceptance of the supplied concrete
word. The legacy `gecode_regular` starts symbols at 1;
`gecode_regular_set` explicitly passes the first symbol and symbol count.
NFA tables contain target-state sets for each row-major state/symbol entry.
Validate states, alphabet/offsets, transitions and final sets. Reachable-state
calculation handles nondeterminism; it supplies no missing word symbol.

<a id="family-023"></a>
**checker-023 — circuits and costs.** Check successor range, permutation and the
single-cycle requirement under each offset convention. Known successors determine
per-arc and total costs in cost forms, using the exact flattened matrix layout and
checked sums. Circuit checking never chooses missing successors.

<a id="family-024"></a>
**checker-024 — legacy scheduling.** Check unary/disjunctive, optional unary,
cumulative and legacy cumulatives under their own fixed/variable duration, usage,
capacity and presence arguments. The currently supported strict disjunctive
relation requires for each pair `start[i]+duration[i] <= start[j]` or its reverse;
a zero-duration task inside an occupied interval conflicts. Standard nonstrict
cumulative empty-task behavior differs from explicit-end native calls. Use event
boundaries for resource checks and do not choose starts or durations.

<a id="family-025"></a>
**checker-025 — explicit-end scheduling.** The five `*_flex` interfaces check
supplied starts, durations, ends and optional presence. Their
[declarations](https://github.com/Gecode/gecode/blob/186551447db0f74639d65cb8de5af190f15ac2c2/gecode/flatzinc/mznlib/gecode_fzn.mzn#L167)
and [handlers](https://github.com/Gecode/gecode/blob/186551447db0f74639d65cb8de5af190f15ac2c2/gecode/flatzinc/registry.cpp#L2081)
separate caller equations `start+duration=end` from resource relations. Unary
zero-duration tasks cannot occur strictly inside another task. Cumulative flex
checks a task's usage at its start, including zero-duration tasks. Multi-machine
cumulatives allow signed usage and enforce upper/lower capacity only during active
time; caller constraints supply nonnegative durations and valid machine indexes.
Optional forms condition caller end equations on presence. No output is selected.

<a id="family-026"></a>
**checker-026 — packing and rectangles.** Check bin loads/capacity, rectangle
separation, touching boundaries, empty dimensions and optional presence. Known bin
placements can calculate load arrays; do not choose bins or coordinates.
Explicit right/top optional forms require separate caller coordinate equations
as documented in `gecode_fzn.mzn`; their native relation must not absorb or drop
those equations. Validate sizes, offsets and checked coordinate sums.

<a id="family-027"></a>
**checker-027 — aggregate/ordered/weighted sets.** Check union, intersection,
partition, disjointness, convexity/hull, sequences, extrema, fixed cardinality with
pairwise intersections of size at most one, and weighted sums. Known sets determine
aggregate sets, hulls, nonempty-set extrema and sums. Empty hull is empty; an empty
Gecode array intersection is the full finite Gecode set universe. Reified extrema
are false for an empty input set. Set sequence order requires every element to
precede all elements of later nonempty sets. Convexity/disjointness alone supply
no missing set.

<a id="family-028"></a>
**checker-028 — set selection and channels.** Check selected union/intersection/
partition, range/roots, integer/set/Boolean channels, inverse sets, sorted channels
and set precedence. Known selected indexes determine an aggregate from only the
selected inputs; an empty intersection uses the explicit `intersect_in` universe
or the Gecode universe. Complete known channel sides can determine the opposite
side under the declared offset/cardinality conventions. Selection never chooses
members or indexes. Inspect the padding and universe restrictions in the
[channel handlers](https://github.com/Gecode/gecode/blob/186551447db0f74639d65cb8de5af190f15ac2c2/gecode/flatzinc/registry.cpp#L2505),
including the excluded zero index in selected-set operations.

<a id="family-029"></a>
**checker-029 — arithmetic and distance extensions.** Check nonnegative gcd
(`gcd(0,0)=0`), divisibility (zero divides only zero), products (empty product 1),
Euclidean modular products (`modulus>0`, result in `0..modulus-1`), integer roots
(floor root, positive degree, negative radicand only for odd degree), pairwise
inter-distance lower bounds and exact minimum-distance matrix relations. Known
operands determine gcd/product/root results; known sites determine argument 4 of
minimum-distance forms. Required-pair bounds are additional relations, not a
witness choice. Validate matrices, symmetry, signs and checked arithmetic using
both `gecode_fzn.mzn` and the
[native mathematical contracts](https://github.com/Gecode/gecode/blob/186551447db0f74639d65cb8de5af190f15ac2c2/gecode/int.hh).

<a id="family-030"></a>
**checker-030 — standard profile closure.** Own every standard source-body and
compiler-intrinsic row, including deprecated, optional, reified and versioned
paths, except direct operation rows assigned above. Provide a small primitive
library/configuration and reproducible offline `--compile` command against these
exact standard sources. Check actual emitted signatures/metadata, aliases,
objective values and definition directions. Operators and compiler intrinsics
can emit operations beyond the explicit call heads shown here, so the static
include scan supplements compile-only acceptance. Close the missing legacy
include edges below; route any new primitive gap to its mathematical owner.

<a id="family-031"></a>
**checker-031 — Gecode profile closure and hook diagnostics.** Own every Gecode
source wrapper and its standard fallback selection, all experimental hook
rejections, and a compile-only configuration using the complete pinned library.
Keep `gecode.mzn`, `gecode_fzn.mzn`, versioned overrides and all mathematical
registrations in scope, including set/float/MPFR forms. Preserve caller equations
and metadata through compilation and report domain tightening/elimination limits.
An installed older library or the current one-file checker override does not
satisfy this profile.

<a id="family-032"></a>
**checker-032 — official FlatZinc-JSON.** Admit the official schema through the
same preparation/type/metadata contracts. It is distinct from prepared-model JSON.

<a id="family-033"></a>
**checker-033 — full acceptance.** Check every indexed row, every selected include
path and both public CLI forms, official JSON and parser-free Wasm. Use focused
native/Wasm report round trips and compile-only direct semantic checks; no solver
build or broad solver matrix is required. No full-support claim is valid while a
mathematical row or a profile include gap lacks working coverage.

## Include gaps and profile obligations

`stdlib.mzn`, `solver_redefinitions.mzn` and `globals.mzn` are the standard roots;
the Gecode roots also include `gecode.mzn`. The helper resolves every explicit
include from every file, not just these roots. MiniZinc searches ordered include
paths before the including file's parent. Gecode overrides precede the standard
directory, and absent overrides fall back to standard files. The compiler also
loads matching `basename.mzn.deprecated.mzn` companions. The index records those
extra edges and all versioned redefinition selections.

The default static closures resolve. Optional legacy decreasing entry points
contain these exact missing include edges in the pinned sources:

| Including file | Absent standard targets | Absent Gecode-profile targets | Mathematical owner | Profile work |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `S/decreasing_bool.mzn` | `fzn_decreasing_bool.mzn`, `fzn_decreasing_bool_reif.mzn` | `fzn_decreasing_bool_reif.mzn` | checker-020 | checker-030 / checker-031 |
| `S/decreasing_float.mzn` | `fzn_decreasing_float.mzn`, `fzn_decreasing_float_reif.mzn` | Both | checker-020 | checker-030 / checker-031 |
| `S/decreasing_int.mzn` | `fzn_decreasing_int.mzn`, `fzn_decreasing_int_reif.mzn` | `fzn_decreasing_int_reif.mzn` | checker-020 | checker-030 / checker-031 |
| `S/decreasing_set.mzn` | `fzn_decreasing_set.mzn`, `fzn_decreasing_set_reif.mzn` | Both | checker-020 | checker-030 / checker-031 |

These wrappers have exact indexed signatures and bodies. The absent files supply
no declaration/signature to extract. The profile tasks must establish a working
path with the same decreasing relation; this inventory does not fabricate a
missing upstream body or count the failed include as support. Other newly missing
include names fail the helper. Gecode supplies the two base Boolean/integer files;
its `_reif`, float and set fallbacks are absent on these legacy paths.

## Grammar, metadata and numeric boundaries

| Boundary | Target and owner | Working subset today |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Text items | checker-011: predicate declarations, fixed parameters, scalar/array variables, aliases, literal initializers, constraints and one satisfy/minimize/maximize solve item; validate type, arity, array shape and declaration order | Boolean, i64 and finite integer sets; signature-checked declarations for the ten current names; ordered items and integer objectives |
| Literals and names | checker-011/015: signed decimal, hexadecimal and octal integers; decimal/exponent floats; Boolean and set literals; flat arrays and references. The grammar separates letter-led predicate identifiers from variable/parameter names that can start with `_`; annotation strings support escapes | Letter/underscore variable names; decimal/hex/octal i64 literals; escaped UTF-8 metadata strings; integer sets; flat `1..n` arrays and earlier references/aliases |
| Annotation expressions | checker-011: nested annotation calls, literals, references and arrays; strings occur in annotations, not mathematical argument slots | Context/role-checked standard/Gecode metadata, nested searches and warm-start arrays; mathematical floats await checker-015 |
| Definitions | checker-011 and each family: validate `is_defined_var`/`defines_var`, aliases and unique directions; check supplied results instead of overwriting | Directions in the current table above |
| Metadata | checker-011: application `checker_value`/`checker_constraint`, `mzn_path`, `mzn_constraint_name`, introduced/defined flags and source fallback; preserve typed IDs/payloads | Application ID, exact integer entity payloads, labels/paths and locations; introduced flags; `computed_domain` excludes its convenience domain from violations/defaults |
| Search/propagation | checker-011/031: search, restart strategy, variable/value selection, consistency strength and Gecode propagation choices are metadata when they preserve the relation. Unknown semantic annotations diagnose | Standard/Gecode variable/value strategies, searches, restarts, warm starts and propagation choices validate without changing feasibility; unknown semantics/hooks diagnose |
| Output selection | checker-011: `output_var`, `output_array`, output sections and introduced flags are metadata; rendering/protocol/search/optimality execution is outside checking | Scalar markers and integer-set dimensions with matching flat cardinality, including non-1-based/multidimensional/empty descriptions; output sections diagnose outside MiniZinc output items |
| Official JSON | checker-032: top-level `version`, `variables`, `arrays`, `constraints`, `output`, `solve`; typed variables, interval domains/sets, literal/reference arrays, annotation call objects and `defines`. Read integer tokens exactly rather than through binary64 | Not accepted |
| Prepared JSON | Existing versioned executable artifact with validated references, shapes, metadata and family operands; values and i64 payloads use exact decimal strings | Accepted through `PreparedModel::from_json`; separate from official FlatZinc-JSON |
| Integers/sets | Each family: checked i64 for values and intermediate arithmetic; compact sorted disjoint integer ranges; explicit division/modulus/overflow errors and domain findings | Working for current operations; no scalar arithmetic wraparound |
| Gecode universes | checker-017/027/028/029: respect explicit extension universes and offsets. `Int::Limits::max=INT_MAX-1`, min its negation; `Set::Limits::max=(Int::Limits::max/2)-1`, min its negation, cardinality `max-min+1` | Current generic set operations use finite i64 sets; wider Gecode extension semantics are planned |
| Floats | checker-015/018: finite binary64 with explicit configurable absolute/relative tolerances and a zero-tolerance strict setting; settle formula/defaults, strict comparisons, domain checks, rounding/conversion and nonfinite/undefined behavior before admission | Mathematical floats reject; finite float literals work only in `restart_geometric` metadata |

On Gecode's 32-bit `int` convention, the explicit integer bounds are
`-2147483646..2147483646` and the set universe is
`-1073741822..1073741822`, with cardinality `2147483645`
([integer constants](https://github.com/Gecode/gecode/blob/186551447db0f74639d65cb8de5af190f15ac2c2/gecode/int.hh#L119),
[set constants](https://github.com/Gecode/gecode/blob/186551447db0f74639d65cb8de5af190f15ac2c2/gecode/set.hh#L95)).
These constants matter for empty aggregate intersections and complement; they do
not replace the general i64 checker contract. Tolerance never supplies a missing
value or rounds an integer payload through a float. Its precise policy is planned
in checker-015, not implemented by this inventory.

## External hooks

checker-031 owns located rejection of the following hooks under pure candidate
checking. They are excluded from mathematical support totals and never count as
satisfied constraints. Their exact source signatures appear in the indexed
`S/experimental/` and `G/experimental/` tables. A source declaration or wrapper does not remove a hook's
search-state meaning.

| Hook surface | Source/dispatch | Required diagnostic behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Standard source APIs `blackbox`, `blackbox_bounds`, `status`, `complete_reif`, `uniform_on_restart`, `last_val`, `sol`; annotations `on_restart`, `propagator`, `propagator_bounds`, `blackbox_exec`, `blackbox_dll` | `S/experimental/blackbox.mzn` and `S/experimental/on_restart.mzn`; overloads/helper signatures are indexed | Reject semantic hooks when they reach checking; compiler helper functions do not establish candidate values |
| `fzn_blackbox`, `gecode_blackbox`, `fzn_blackbox_bounds`, `gecode_blackbox_bounds`, plus all three literal registry prefix spellings for each registered Gecode name | `experimental/blackbox/`; `p_blackbox`/`p_blackbox_bounds`; `blackbox_exec(target[,args])` and `blackbox_dll(target[,args])` execution annotations | Reject the located call/annotation: external executable or DLL execution is unsupported in pure checking |
| `fzn_on_restart_status`, `gecode_on_restart_status`, `fzn_on_restart_complete`, `gecode_on_restart_complete` | `experimental/on_restart/`; special parser dispatch | Reject the located call: restart status/history is unavailable in pure checking |
| `fzn_on_restart_last_val_TYPE`, `gecode_on_restart_last_val_TYPE`, `fzn_on_restart_sol_TYPE`, `gecode_on_restart_sol_TYPE` for each of `bool`, `int`, `float`, `set` | Source wrappers and `gecode/flatzinc/parser.yxx` dispatch, outside `Registry::add` | Same located search-history diagnostic |
| `fzn_on_restart_uniform_int`, `gecode_on_restart_uniform_int`, `fzn_on_restart_uniform_float`, `gecode_on_restart_uniform_float` | Source wrappers and parser restart dispatch | Same located diagnostic; do not draw a random candidate value |

Ordinary solve restart/search annotations such as `relax_and_reconstruct` are
metadata; a mathematical predicate that reads restart history is an excluded
hook. The [parser's special dispatch](https://github.com/Gecode/gecode/blob/186551447db0f74639d65cb8de5af190f15ac2c2/gecode/flatzinc/parser.yxx#L1576)
explains why registry counts alone miss restart hooks. Seven upstream EOF
prototypes are malformed because they lack a terminating semicolon:
`gecode_on_restart_last_val_bool`,
`gecode_on_restart_last_val_float`, `gecode_on_restart_last_val_int`,
`gecode_on_restart_last_val_set`, `gecode_on_restart_sol_float`,
`gecode_on_restart_status` and `gecode_on_restart_uniform_float`. The scanner
indexes their exact signatures and marks the missing delimiter; it does not
claim those source files compile.

## Registration counts and conditions

The pinned file has **315 textual** `registry().add` matches with **311 unique
literal strings**. Three matches are commented out: `float_cosh`, `float_sinh` and
`float_tanh`. A comment-aware scan finds **312 active statements** and **308 unique
literal names**, producing **924 unique accepted spellings** across all feature
conditions after prefix expansion. Duplicate active statements include
`array_int_maximum` and the three `set_in` spellings selected by opposite set-feature branches. The registry
table keeps the statement, handler and guard rather than deduplicating them.

`Registry::add(id,p)` installs `id`, `gecode_ + id` and `fzn_ + id` literally
([implementation](https://github.com/Gecode/gecode/blob/186551447db0f74639d65cb8de5af190f15ac2c2/gecode/flatzinc/registry.cpp#L70)).
Thus `gecode_gcd_int` also registers `gecode_gecode_gcd_int` and
`fzn_gecode_gcd_int`; no prefix is stripped. Set and float guards and the nested
MPFR guard describe this upstream build surface. Every mathematical row stays in
the checker target regardless of those flags. Signature overloads, source-only
wrappers, these aliases and the compiler's include selection are distinct facts;
none of the counts proves full coverage.

## Source signatures and decomposition calls

Signatures preserve fixed/variable types, dimensions, argument order and declaration annotations; whitespace outside strings is collapsed. A source body is `wrapper`, with its explicit call heads listed (operators and compiler lowering also contribute). `declaration` rows link source definitions by name; overload selection still belongs to MiniZinc. Profile-specific `direct` rows need runtime evaluation; `intrinsic` rows belong to compiler elaboration. None of these routes counts as working support unless `Now` says `C`. Each file heading links the exact semantic source, with the line in each row; direct Gecode semantics also use the registry handler and family notes.
